articles.title: Human remains identified as mum missing since 2019
articles.summary: A 56-year-old man is arrested after the remains of Joanne Sheen were found almost seven years after she went missing.
articles.body:
Human remains discovered in woodland in south-west London following a wildfire have been identified as a woman who has been missing since 2019.

Mother-of-three Joanne Sheen, then aged 44, was last seen when she travelled from Fareham to Southampton with a friend on 5 December 2019.

Metropolitan Police officers were called to Padstow Walk in Feltham on 12 August after bones were discovered in an area of shrubland damaged by a fire the previous week.

A 56-year-old man from Southampton has been arrested on suspicion of conspiracy to commit murder and he remains in police custody.

Detectives in London have now handed the investigation over to Hampshire Police after the remains were identified as those of Sheen.

Sheen's disappearance sparked a major police investigation, which the force described as "long and complex".

Police said they had followed more than 4,000 lines of inquiry, taken more than 300 statements and carried out detailed searches at more than 10 addresses and on numerous vessels.

Det Ch Insp Toby Elcock, from the Major Crime Team, said: "While this tragic discovery is not the outcome Joanne's family, or any of us, had hoped for, we hope the identification of her remains can at least begin to provide some answers after many years of uncertainty.

"Throughout this investigation, Joanne's family have shown tremendous strength and dignity in the face of unimaginable circumstances, and our thoughts remain with them at this incredibly difficult time.

"As our investigation progresses, we remain committed to establishing exactly what happened to Joanne and ensuring that those responsible are held accountable."

He stressed that the police would still like to hear from anyone with information about Sheen's disappearance.

London Fire Brigade was called on 5 August to a blaze that damaged about two hectares of shrubland in an area known as Bedfont Pits.

The human remains were discovered a week later, and a post-mortem examination suggested they had come from a woman aged between 25 and 45.

A Metropolitan Police spokesman confirmed the remains were found by a member of the public at the site close to Bedfont Lakes Country Park.

Crimestoppers has agreed to reinstate a £20,000 reward for information that supports the investigation.

Sheen was reported missing by her family in February 2020 - two months after she was last seen.

Several people were arrested on suspicion of conspiracy to murder in 2020, but no charges were brought and the investigation remained unsolved.

Police previously said she did not have a permanent place of address, a vehicle or a bank account.

articles.title: Why Christian Pulisic left off USMNT's roster by Mauricio Pochettino
articles.summary: As fans tune in to see the U.S. men's national team compete in official matches for the first time since the 2026 FIFA World Cup, many familiar faces are abs...
articles.body:
As fans tune in to see the U.S. men's national team compete in official matches for the first time since the 2026 FIFA World Cup, a number of new faces will be present.

With that, a host of well-known superstars will not be amongst the 28 players convening for USMNT camp this September, led by superstar Christian Pulisic .

The 27-year-old was not included on the squad of players called up by Mauricio Pochettino for friendly games against Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada across the next two weeks in a combined four-match international break.

The Sporting News explains why Pulisic was not brought in to the national team camp, and why those who are present on the roster were called up instead.

Why was Christian Pulisic left off USMNT roster for fall 2026?

A combination of fitness and roster selection preferences left USMNT superstar Christian Pulisic off the roster for the four matches in September and October of 2026.

Pulisic has only just returned from an injury suffered in the World Cup earlier this summer, yet to start a single match for AC Milan .

Additionally, Mauricio Pochettino has called in a youthful squad for the coming four friendlies, leaving other regular stars like Folarin Balogun , Tim Weah and Brenden Aaronson on the sidelines in favor of young talents like Cavan Sullivan , Julian Hall and Justin Ellis , amongst many others.

Pochettino told reporters upon unveiling the roster that he was specifically targeting the 2028 Olympics with his roster selection, hoping to get a number of top U-23 eligible players some senior national team experience to help build them for a gold medal run two years down the road in Los Angeles.

So, with the combination of his recovering fitness and the youth movement, there was no place for Pulisic on the roster. He will use the two weeks off to rest, recover and prepare for the next run of matches for his club team, with Milan set to return to action against Sassuolo on October 11 before a Europa League visit to RB Leipzig four days later.

Christian Pulisic is not currently injured, but he has also recently returned from injury and therefore is not fully fit, at least according to AC Milan boss Ruben Amorim.

The 27-year-old suffered a microfracture in his lower leg in the World Cup defeat to Belgium earlier this summer, U.S. Soccer confirmed in the aftermath of the team's exit from the competition on home soil. Pulisic was injured early in the second half when he went to take a shot but instead kicked the back of Youri Tielemans ' leg.

He was eventually replaced in the 59th minute by Sebastian Berhalter , a major blow to the United States, who were ultimately beaten handily by their European opponents.

The injury left Pulisic sidelined for several weeks, disrupting the start of the 2026/27 club season with AC Milan. Pulisic was absent for all of preseason and was an unused substitute for Milan's first three Serie A matches of the new campaign.

Pulisic finally returned to action with 45 minutes off the bench against Lazio on September 12, and then again playing the full second half in a 2-0 defeat to Benfica in the Europa League four days later. He has not yet started a match for Milan.

USMNT roster for September, October international break

Pochettino called in 28 players for the September and October friendlies against Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada. The normal size of the roster is 26, but with four matches in this window instead of the usual two, he has decided to bring a few extra players to spread the load, account for injuries and take advantage of the extra minutes.

Below is the confirmed roster for the U.S. men's national team for the coming fall international break, which was announced Thursday, September 16.

There are a slew of uncapped players, 13 in total, with eight teenagers and 12 players on the roster eligible to play in the 2028 Olympics.

articles.title: How fantasy fans are keeping a Turkish blacksmithing tradition alive
articles.summary: In Izmir’s historic Kemeralti bazaar, the Akdemir family is finding new customers for a four-generation craft.
articles.body:
Kemeralti Bazaar, Izmir, Turkiye – To the casual passer-by, the Akdemir family’s workshop could be any traditional blacksmith’s forge. Dozens of hammers and tongs hang from the walls; kebab skewers, knives and axes lie across the benches; a length of steel glows in the fire. But for those familiar with fantasy worlds and gaming, a second look may be required.

Just a few steps inside the workshop's shutter-style doors, an enormous forged fantasy sword rests across a countertop, similar to the one wielded by the Lich King in the popular video game World of Warcraft. Elsewhere are weapons inspired by TV series and video games, including Game of Thrones and League of Legends, rendered in steel.

At the forge, Suleyman Akdemir, a large man with a furrowed brow, grips a glowing length of metal with long tongs, draws it from the fire, and lays it across the anvil. A few metres away, his father, Omer, 54, reaches for a tool. Then the power hammer crashes down, its blows reverberating through the narrow workshop and out into the covered streets of Izmir’s Kemeralti bazaar, forcing conversation to wait.

Suleyman, 30, wears a brown leather apron over a black T-shirt, his hands encased in black gloves. His father rarely stops working while he talks; Suleyman often pauses, turning towards his customers before returning to the forge.

Between father and son, exchanges are calm, almost formal. Here, they seem less like family than two craftsmen who have spent years learning how to work around one another.

When the hammer falls silent, Suleyman turns from the forge.

“Ever since I was a child. I’d say since I first learned to walk, I've been working here with hot forging,” he says, breaking into a smile.

The surroundings bear that history. The fantasy weapons are newcomers to a workshop where Suleyman's family has practised blacksmithing for generations. Yet, incongruous as they look among the agricultural tools and barbecue skewers, they may be one reason the forge is still running.

“Thank God, we can make anything we see,” Suleyman says.

That conviction has taken the Akdemirs somewhere his predecessors could hardly have imagined. Customers from around the world now send Suleyman images and ideas inspired by weapons they have seen on screen, which he interprets as individually designed, hand-forged pieces.

articles.title: Syria arrests five former al-Assad-era officers over strikes on civilians
articles.summary: Former air officers, including an air force general, were arrested in a series of operations.
articles.body:
Syrian security forces say they have arrested five former air force officers accused of involvement in air strikes on civilians during the rule of deposed President Bashar al-Assad.

The former officers, including an air force general, were arrested in a series of operations in coordination with the Counter Terrorism Directorate, the head of Syria’s Internal Security Forces in the coastal Tartous province said in a statement on Friday.

The detained officers were involved “in using the air force, airbases and field command centres to conduct intensive combat airstrikes targeting populated areas”, according to the statement.

Colonel Abdul Aal Mohammad Abdul Aal said the detainees included pilots, field commanders and officers who served in operations rooms under the former regime.

Those detained were identified as Major-General Mohammad Fajr Ali; Brigadier-General pilot Abdullah Ali Mualla; Colonel pilot Nidal Hussein Saleh; Colonel Mohammad Ali Salim; and Lieutenant-Colonel pilot Talib Abdul Karim Hassan.

Investigations and military records indicated that the five, each according to his position and responsibilities, were involved in planning, directing and carrying out air strikes, Abdul Aal said.

According to the security chief, aircraft, airbases and field command centres were used to conduct intensive strikes on populated areas, resulting in the destruction of residential neighbourhoods and infrastructure, forced displacement and extensive casualties.

The forces said investigations were ongoing before the suspects’ referral for trial.

Over more than 13 years of a civil war that claimed more than half a million lives, Syrian forces relentlessly shelled areas held by the rebels before al-Assad was toppled and the current government came to power.

Since al-Assad was overthrown in December 2024, Syria’s new government has arrested dozens of former security officials.

Earlier this month, Syrian authorities said they had arrested nine former pilots, including three generals accused of taking part in lethal bombings of towns and villages under al-Assad’s rule.

Syria sentenced Bashar al-Assad, his brother Maher al-Assad, and five other security officials to death in absentia in August for atrocities committed during the civil war.

The former president fled Syria as his government fell and is believed to be living in Russia.
